children: shares gained more than 2% in premarket trading after Raymond James initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and an $80 price target, implying roughly 29% upside. Analyst Brian Gesuale sees Rocket Lab evolving beyond its small-launch roots into a vertically integrated space company, with Neutron, spacecraft systems and improving cash flow potentially driving its next stage of growth.

Rocket Lab provides launch services through its Electron rocket while also selling spacecraft, satellite components, payload systems and optical communications technology. That broader model gives the company several potential revenue streams beyond simply sending satellites into orbit.

The bullish call comes as Rocket Lab continues building launch momentum. The company completed its 16th Electron mission of 2026 on Sept. 11, deploying an Earth-observation satellite into low Earth orbit for a confidential customer. The flight marked Rocket Lab's 95th launch overall, with another commercial Electron mission planned before the end of September.

Gesuale sees that launch record as only part of the story. He views Rocket Lab as an emerging vertically integrated space platform spanning launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications. Neutron, its planned medium-lift rocket, is expected to expand those capabilities in 2027.
RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads, and optical communications, Gesuale said.
The analyst also expects Rocket Lab's financial profile to improve as investment requirements decline. He projects positive EBITDA and free cash flow around 2027 to 2028.

Neutron is the most important catalyst. Successful development and commercial deployment could move Rocket Lab into the larger medium-lift launch market and materially expand its addressable opportunity.

Investors should also monitor Electron launch cadence, progress toward positive free cash flow and integration of acquired businesses. Rocket Lab's $155.3 million Mynaric acquisition expands its laser-communications capabilities, but Gesuale flagged integration as a risk.

If Neutron stays on schedule while launch activity and space-systems revenue grow, Raymond James' bullish thesis could strengthen. Delays, acquisition problems or continued heavy cash consumption would make that $80 target harder to reach.

title: Raymond James Has Strong Message For Rocket Lab Investors
